_about: The one list of forecast systems and how they are grouped, in the working paper's five groups. scripts/build.py renders the forecast systems table on the accuracy page from it. `id` is the series' id in the accuracy files; a system scored twice has a row for each series.

groups.title: Prediction market
groups.note: The system every other row is compared against.

systems.name: ForecastEx prediction market
systems.what: Daily contracts on each city’s high and low temperature. The ladder of Yes prices across strikes is a probability distribution for the settle, and its central value, where the ladder crosses fifty cents, is scored as one value.

groups.title: Station MOS
groups.note: Statistical guidance fitted at the settlement station itself, from model output corrected against what the models got wrong there in the past. These are left as issued by the bias correction. GFS MOS, NAM MOS and the NBM station guidance appear twice, on the daytime maximum each issues and on its hourly temperature rows.

systems.name: LAMP
systems.what: LAMP, statistical guidance refreshed with the latest observations.

systems.name: NBM station MOS, issued maximum
systems.what: The station text bulletin of the National Blend of Models, read on its own daytime maximum, the highest temperature its TXN row expects from 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time, and scored against the National Weather Service climate report on the location-days whose report puts the maximum inside that window.

systems.name: NBM station MOS, hourly rows
systems.what: The same bulletin read on its hourly temperature rows, the extreme of the hours left in the day, and scored against the METAR settle.

systems.name: GFS MOS, issued maximum
systems.what: Statistical guidance built on the GFS alone, with no forecaster editing, read on its own daytime maximum, the X/N row’s highest temperature from 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time, and scored against the climate report on the location-days whose report puts the maximum inside that window.

systems.name: GFS MOS, hourly rows
systems.what: The same bulletin read on its hourly temperature rows, the extreme of the hours left in the day, and scored against the METAR settle.

systems.name: NAM MOS, issued maximum
systems.what: Statistical guidance built on NOAA’s North American Mesoscale model, read on its own daytime maximum, the X/N row’s highest temperature from 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time, and scored against the climate report on the location-days whose report puts the maximum inside that window. NCEP retired the model and this guidance at 1200 UTC on 3 November 2026 (service change notice 26-47), so the series ends with 2 November, the last day it covered whole. The Rapid Refresh Forecast System that replaces the model issues no station bulletin, so no successor carries the record on.

systems.name: NAM MOS, hourly rows
systems.what: The same bulletin read on its hourly temperature rows, the extreme of the hours left in the day, and scored against the METAR settle. NCEP retired the model and this guidance at 1200 UTC on 3 November 2026 (service change notice 26-47), so the series ends with 2 November, the last day it covered whole. The Rapid Refresh Forecast System that replaces the model issues no station bulletin, so no successor carries the record on.

systems.name: DWD MOSMIX
systems.what: MOSMIX, which combines and corrects the German and European models station by station.
systems.grid: The settlement airport’s station in DWD’s list, which lacks Buckley Field, Houston Hobby and Chicago Midway

groups.title: Blend
groups.note: A calibrated blend of many models on a fine grid.

systems.name: National Blend of Models, METAR
systems.what: NOAA’s calibrated blend of many models, the starting point for the Weather Service’s own forecast.

systems.name: National Blend of Models, URMA
systems.what: The same Blend scored a second time, as issued, against URMA, the Weather Service’s gridded analysis, at the grid box holding the station, its daily value against the largest analysis over the station-local day. Highs only.

groups.title: Human-edited
groups.note: Forecasters editing model guidance with their own judgment.

systems.name: National Weather Service, climate report
systems.what: The official public forecast from the National Digital Forecast Database, which forecasters edit starting from the National Blend of Models. Its high is a daytime maximum for 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time and its low an overnight minimum for 7 PM to 8 AM, assigned to the morning the night ends, while the contracts settle on the calendar day.
systems.updates: About twice a day, amended as needed

systems.name: National Weather Service, URMA
systems.what: The same forecast scored a second time, as issued, against URMA, the Weather Service’s gridded analysis, at the grid box holding the station, its daytime maximum against the largest analysis over 7 AM to 7 PM local standard time. Highs only.
systems.updates: About twice a day, amended as needed

groups.title: Artificial intelligence
groups.note: Models trained on decades of past weather rather than stepping physical equations forward.

systems.name: ECMWF AIFS ens. mean
systems.what: AIFS, ECMWF’s machine-learning forecasting system. Live, it is the 51-member ensemble. Its single value is the extreme of the ensemble’s hourly means over the hours left in the day, the median of its distribution, and the members’ spread gives the distribution. Before live capture began the forecast archive holds its single deterministic run.

groups.title: Raw numerical weather prediction
groups.note: Physics models that step the atmosphere forward in time. Their output applies to a grid box rather than the exact point where a station sits, which the bias correction addresses.

systems.name: NOAA HRRR
systems.what: NOAA’s High-Resolution Rapid Refresh, covering the contiguous United States.

systems.name: ECMWF IFS
systems.what: ECMWF’s global model, the IFS, as one deterministic run. Before live capture began the record uses ECMWF’s 0.25° open data from the forecast archive, and from then on a data provider’s high-resolution series, whose grid spacing could not be confirmed.
systems.grid: 0.25°, about 25 km, in the archive, not confirmed for the live series

systems.name: ECMWF IFS ens. mean
systems.what: Described by the data provider as the average of ECMWF’s 51-member ensemble, which could not be independently confirmed. Only its mean is used here.

systems.name: NOAA GFS
systems.what: NOAA’s Global Forecast System. Before live capture began the record comes from a forecast archive that returns HRRR within 48 hours of the run.

systems.name: NOAA GEFS median
systems.what: NOAA’s Global Ensemble Forecast System, 31 members. Its median, the extreme of the hourly ensemble means over the hours left in the day, is scored as one value beside the systems, and its spread as a distribution.

systems.name: DWD ICON
systems.what: ICON, the global model of Germany’s weather service.

systems.name: DWD ICON-EPS median
systems.what: ICON’s global ensemble, 40 members. Its median is scored as one value beside the systems, and its spread as a distribution.

systems.name: ECCC GEM
systems.what: GEM, the model of Environment and Climate Change Canada, as a seamless series that uses its regional and high-resolution configurations at US stations.

systems.name: ECCC GEPS median
systems.what: Canada’s global ensemble, 21 members. Its median is scored as one value beside the systems, and its spread as a distribution.

systems.name: Met Office UM
systems.what: The Met Office Unified Model, run globally.

systems.name: Météo-France ARPEGE
systems.what: ARPEGE, the global model of Météo-France.

systems.name: JMA GSM
systems.what: The Global Spectral Model of the Japan Meteorological Agency.
